newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN begins crisis meeting over Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN begins crisis meeting over Cambodia.

text.p: Foreign ministers from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Thursday began an emergency meeting to discuss strife-torn Cambodia and its application for membership in the grouping.

"Everything related to Cambodia will be discussed including membership (in ASEAN)...and including life and properties (in Cambodia)," Philippines Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon told reporters just before the meeting started.

ASEAN was to induct Cambodia, along with Burma and Laos, as the final members of the grouping at its annual meeting at the end of this month in Kuala Lumpur. But Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's bloody power grab over the weekend has cast considerable doubt over those plans.

Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi told reporters late on Monday there should be no confusion about the decision to admit Cambodia into ASEAN and the timing of its entry. "We will be very practical and pragmatic about it."

Abdullah pointedly did not reiterate Malaysia's oft-stated position that the three new members should be inducted at the July meeting, which will celebrate the 30th anniversary of the founding of ASEAN.
Malaysia is this year's chairman of ASEAN, which also includes Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
